b: Been a Claude user since January. Love it. Love Claude Code, but I particularly love Claude Cowork. Letting it run wild in my computer is amazing.

Also been a Cursor user for a few years. Loved it, but once I started using Claude, I figured it was redundant. I planned to stop using it once my subscription lapsed. Unfortunately, I had automatic subscription on, so I unknowingly paid for another full year in July. So, fuck it, right? I've got it, I might as well use it.

My workflow is now: I use Opus for brainstorming, planning, and code review. Opus creates a detailed prompt for Cursor, and Cursor does the dirty work. Claude never actually writes any code, so I save my tokens for the brainy stuff. And once in a while, Cursor even catches something that Claude missed. This has been the revelation; it's almost like having a second opinion, or a second set of eyes on stuff.

I liked this combo so much, I built a bridge program that lets Claude Desktop interact directly with Cursor via the API. Now, I talk to Claude from anywhere, over my phone. When we're ready, Claude gives the orders to Cursor, keeps an eye on things, reviews code at predetermined checkpoints, and reports back to me. Cowork can't access the terminal from its sandbox, but Cursor can, so I even built a messaging feature where Cursor can send me a permission request for sensitive terminal commands over Telegram. Now I'm building from anywhere and I've never been more productive or efficient.
I'm really curious if I'm the only one who uses this tandem. I imagine the vast majority of people just use Claude Code, but I can't be the only one doing this... right?
